questions.question: When downshifting, you should:

options.text: Shift through multiple gears at once.
Shift through one gear at a time.
Always shift to neutral first.
Accelerate.

questions.correctAnswerText: Shift through one gear at a time.
questions.explanation: When downshifting, move down one gear at a time. Release the clutch slowly between each gear change.

questions.question: Head and neck injuries can be reduced by:

options.text: Wearing a helmet.
Wearing a leather jacket.
Using the rear brake only.
Wearing goggles.

questions.correctAnswerText: Wearing a helmet.
questions.explanation: A good helmet greatly reduces head and neck injuries. A helmet is your best protection if you crash.

questions.question: When it is obvious that you are going to turn, you:

options.text: Do not need to use a turn signal.
Should still use a turn signal.
Only need to use a turn signal if pedestrians are nearby.
Only need to use a turn signal at a stop light.

questions.correctAnswerText: Should still use a turn signal.
questions.explanation: Always use a turn signal when you turn or change lanes, even if you think it is obvious. Other vehicles may be hidden from view. Always signal to keep others safe.

questions.question: A motorcycle operator can slow down by:

options.text: Downshifting.
Upshifting.
Cross-shifting.
Rolling on the throttle.

questions.correctAnswerText: Downshifting.
questions.explanation: Downshifting is a common way to slow down on a motorcycle. Note that downshifting does not turn on the brake lights.

questions.question: Which type of sign is yellow with black lettering or symbols?

options.text: Warning
Service
Regulatory
Speed limit

questions.correctAnswerText: Warning
questions.explanation: Warning signs are yellow with black lettering or symbols. They tell drivers about road conditions ahead.

questions.question: It is a good idea to wear reflective clothing:

options.text: At night.
During the day.
At dusk.
All of the above.

questions.correctAnswerText: All of the above.
questions.explanation: Wear reflective and bright clothing at all times when riding. Crashes happen both day and night, so stay visible whenever you ride.

questions.question: The single most important thing you can do to improve your chances of surviving a crash is to:

options.text: Wear a high-quality helmet that is securely fastened.
Wear shorts.
Wear sneakers.
Wear goggles.

questions.correctAnswerText: Wear a high-quality helmet that is securely fastened.
questions.explanation: Wearing a high-quality helmet that is fastened properly is the best way to survive a crash.

questions.question: When riding with a passenger, you should:

options.text: Assume the passenger has ridden a motorcycle before.
Not assume the passenger has ridden before and explain what to do.
Not let them ask questions.
Not explain anything since they are only a passenger.

questions.correctAnswerText: Not assume the passenger has ridden before and explain what to do.
questions.explanation: A passenger needs to know how to ride safely. Never assume they know what to do. Give complete instructions before every ride.

questions.question: If only one alcoholic drink is consumed:

options.text: Judgment and riding abilities can still be affected.
There is usually no effect on the body.
The effect only lasts a short time.
The effect can be removed by drinking coffee.

questions.correctAnswerText: Judgment and riding abilities can still be affected.
questions.explanation: Even one drink can affect judgment and riding skills. Only time will remove alcohol from your body. Coffee does not help.

questions.question: When riding in a group:

options.text: The group should be large.
Inexperienced riders should lead.
Inexperienced riders should ride just behind the leaders.
Riders should pair up.

questions.correctAnswerText: Inexperienced riders should ride just behind the leaders.
questions.explanation: Inexperienced riders should stay near the front, just behind the leader, so experienced riders can watch them. Keep groups small to avoid separation. Pairing up is unsafe because riders cannot escape easily.

questions.question: If you borrow a motorcycle, what should you do?

options.text: Do not worry about checking the tire pressure.
Expect it to handle the same as your own bike.
The lender will check the brakes, so you don't have to.
Stay farther away from other vehicles to give yourself more time to stop.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stay farther away from other vehicles to give yourself more time to stop.
questions.explanation: When you borrow a motorcycle, check it just like you would check your own bike. Ride carefully on an unfamiliar motorcycle and keep extra space between you and other vehicles when stopping.

questions.question: You have been drinking alcohol. If you wait one hour for each drink before riding, what could still happen?

options.text: You cannot be arrested for drinking and riding.
Your riding skills will not be affected.
Alcohol effects may still remain in your body.
You will be fine as long as you ride slowly.

questions.correctAnswerText: Alcohol effects may still remain in your body.
questions.explanation: Your body can get rid of about one drink per hour. But alcohol can build up in your body even if you have just one drink per hour. Your skills and judgment can still be impaired.

questions.question: What should you wear to help other drivers see you?

options.text: Dark-colored clothes.
Bright-colored clothes.
Lights.
A black jacket.

questions.correctAnswerText: Bright-colored clothes.
questions.explanation: Wear bright-colored clothes so other drivers can see you. Bright colors help you be visible both during the day and at night.

questions.question: What kind of footwear should you choose for riding?

options.text: Shoes with long heels.
Shoes with long laces that hang loose.
Shoes that cover your ankles.
Shoes made from thin materials.

questions.correctAnswerText: Shoes that cover your ankles.
questions.explanation: Wear boots or shoes that are tall and strong enough to cover and support your ankles. Heels should be short so they don't get caught. Laces should be tucked in so they don't get caught on the motorcycle.

questions.question: How should you check your tire pressure?

options.text: Look at the tire to see if it looks full.
Use a tire gauge.
Squeeze the tire with your hand.
Compare your tire height to another tire.

questions.correctAnswerText: Use a tire gauge.
questions.explanation: Use a tire gauge to check your tire pressure before every ride. A tire can look okay even if it is under-inflated, so looking at it is not enough.

questions.question: What should you do to reduce the chance of a crash?

options.text: Make sure other drivers can see you.
Keep other drivers guessing about where you are going.
Always ride very close to other vehicles.
Ride on the shoulder of the road.

questions.correctAnswerText: Make sure other drivers can see you.
questions.explanation: To reduce crashes, be visible to other drivers. Use your signals, brake light, and lane position to show your plans. Keep space around your motorcycle and watch the road ahead, behind, and beside you.

questions.question: Which clothing item will NOT help prevent injuries in a crash?

options.text: Heavy shoes
Full-length pants
Shorts
Full-fingered gloves

questions.correctAnswerText: Shorts
questions.explanation: To reduce injury, wear a helmet, eye protection, heavy shoes or boots, full-length pants, a jacket, and full-fingered gloves. Choose clothes made of tough materials for the best protection.

questions.question: How many brakes do most motorcycles have?

options.text: Only a front brake.
Only a rear brake.
A front brake and a rear brake.
A front brake, a rear brake, and an emergency brake.

questions.correctAnswerText: A front brake and a rear brake.
questions.explanation: Most motorcycles have two brakes: one for the front wheel and one for the rear wheel.

questions.question: What are the rules about passing in a no passing zone?

options.text: A motorcycle may still pass another vehicle.
A motorcycle cannot pass another vehicle.
A motorcycle may pass if it is done quickly before another car comes.
A motorcycle may pass on the shoulder.

questions.correctAnswerText: A motorcycle cannot pass another vehicle.
questions.explanation: Passing is not allowed in no passing zones. You also cannot pass by riding off the main road.

questions.question: What does keeping space between your motorcycle and other vehicles do?

options.text: Gives you time to react if another driver makes a mistake.
Keeps you stuck in one spot in your lane.
Lets you rely on other drivers to find hazards.
Means you must ride faster to keep up with traffic.

questions.correctAnswerText: Gives you time to react if another driver makes a mistake.
questions.explanation: Keeping space around your motorcycle helps you have time and room to react if another driver makes a mistake.

questions.question: Why should motorcycle riders turn their heads to look over their shoulders before changing lanes?

options.text: Motorcycles have blind spots, just like other vehicles.
They can catch the attention of other drivers by turning their heads.
Mirrors are not really helpful.
They should try to make eye contact with surrounding drivers.

questions.correctAnswerText: Motorcycles have blind spots, just like other vehicles.
questions.explanation: Motorcycles have blind spots that mirrors cannot show. Always turn your head to check for vehicles or hazards in your blind spot before changing lanes.

questions.question: Why should you wear riding gloves?

options.text: You should not wear them because they make your hands too hot.
They give you a better grip on the handgrips.
You should not wear them because they make controls harder to use.
Wear them only on cooler days.

questions.correctAnswerText: They give you a better grip on the handgrips.
questions.explanation: Leather gloves should be worn while riding. They improve your grip on the handgrips and protect your hands if you crash.

questions.question: If hazards are on your left, where should you ride in your lane?

options.text: In the left portion of the lane.
In the right portion of the lane.
In any portion of the lane.
On the shoulder.

questions.correctAnswerText: In the right portion of the lane.
questions.explanation: When hazards are on your left, ride in the right portion of the lane. Change your position as road and traffic conditions change.

questions.question: What is one benefit of regular motorcycle maintenance?

options.text: Your motorcycle will ride well for a long time.
Maintenance checks take very little time.
Maintenance will be inexpensive.
Maintenance checks can help prevent parking tickets.

questions.correctAnswerText: Your motorcycle will ride well for a long time.
questions.explanation: A motorcycle will continue to ride like new if you maintain it properly and perform routine inspections regularly.

questions.question: Which sign is rectangular?

options.text: School crossing sign.
Railroad crossing sign.
Stop sign.
Speed limit sign.

questions.correctAnswerText: Speed limit sign.
questions.explanation: Speed limit signs and other regulatory signs are rectangular and white with black lettering. You must follow the rules shown on these signs.
